tone_statements.quote: 2.3. Tones I have distinguished the following 5 contour tones for Hezhang Buyi, which are: 33 – mid level 55 – high level 21 – low falling 35 – rising 53 – high falling Most Gelao dialects in western Guizhou have 4 or 5 tones (He 1983), while Kam-Sui languages in southeastern Guizhou around 8 tones (Diller, et al. 2008).

tone_statements.citation: Wu Wenyi, Wil C. Snyder & Liang Yongshu. 2007. Survey of the Guizhou Bouyei Language. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 2007-001. Dallas: SIL International.
tone_statements.quote: Tones Category 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 Pitch value 24 42 52 31 35 33 35 34 … The realizations of the tone categories can be summed up as follows: • Tone 1 is either low-rising or mid-even. A few places have high-rising. • Tone 2 is normally low-falling … • Tone 3 is often mid-even … • Tone 4 is normally high-falling … • Tone 5 is often high-rising … • Tone 6 has all varied contours, no main tendency. • Tone 7 is almost always high-rising. • Tone 8 is varied. • Tone 9 is normally merged with tone 7 … • Tone 10 is normally merged with tone 8, though some places have various other contours.

tone.says: Wangmo Fuxi lect: eight tones, 24, 42, 52, 31, 35, 33 plus 35 and 34 on (historically) stop-final syllables; levels and contours. Across 24 Guizhou lects the ten Tai categories surface as 6-10 tones.

sources.note: Section 2.3 states five contour tones for Hezhang Buyi - 33 mid level, 55 high level, 21 low falling, 35 rising, 53 high falling - based on ~170 elicited words (phonology explicitly 'tentative'); compares with 4-5 tones in western Guizhou Gelao and ~8 in Kam-Sui; all forms in the text and the Appendix 1 word list (4 Buyi lects) carry Chao tone numbers.
